title: First-party scene and graphics library inspired by proven web 3D ergonomics
question: Which layered W library can retain Three.js-like scene productivity while enabling native ownership, specialization, provider portability, and whole-product optimization?
scope: scene, animation, material, asset, and render-graph vocabulary
dense data and resource ownership direction
incremental executable witnesses and performance axes
crosspoints: fixed arrays, views, matrices, SIMD, and numeric modes
virtual objects, ownership, tasks, and resource lifecycle
accelerator domains, kernels, shader lowering, and providers
std.presentation, image buffers, and asset packaging
registry reachability and signed binary distribution
benchmarkReason: This package records a design candidate and future witness plan; it contains no compiled graphics product or performance result.

officialRefs.claim: Three.js composes a renderer, scene graph, camera, geometry, material, texture, and lights over lower-level WebGL.
Three.js treats a local-space hierarchy as its central scene composition model.
Three.js animation includes clips, actions, mixers, blending, bones, morph targets, and grouped state.
Three.js keeps controls, loaders, and post-processing as separately imported addons.
The glTF loader returns scenes, cameras, and animations and composes optional decoders and format extensions.
Three.js applications must explicitly dispose textures, geometries, materials, and other graphics resources.
WebGPURenderer targets WebGPU, can fall back to WebGL2, and integrates the node-based shader system.
The WebGPU post-processing path supports MRT and combines compatible node effects to reduce passes.
Three.js publishes separate core, addon, WebGPU, and shader-node entrypoints and maintains a tree-shaking test.
MLIR GPU is a middle-level kernel, launch, and binary abstraction rather than a complete graphics host API.
MLIR provides a SPIR-V dialect and conversions while host resource management remains external.
MLIR virtual vectors preserve target-independent vector semantics before lower-level specialization.

stopCondition: Stop if the candidate requires one physical object per scene node, hides resource lifetime, grants ambient I/O, couples portable semantics to one graphics API, silently falls back between providers, or claims implementation or performance without a real product witness.
